common_name: Young shrub with toothed leaves (not stevia)
scientific_name: Not identified (not Stevia: the leaves are not sweet)
id_basis: Thin, woody brown stems with opposite pairs of light-green leaves that narrow to the base and are coarsely toothed toward the tip. That fits stevia. A taste test settles it: stevia leaves are intensely sweet.

Thin, woody brown stems with opposite pairs of light-green leaves that narrow to the base and are coarsely toothed toward the tip. It was taken for stevia, but the leaves have no sweetness at all (taste test, October 23), so it is not stevia. A square stem would point to the mint family (salvia); a round one to a hydrangea cutting or a eupatorium.
id_alternatives:
Hydrangea cutting
Salvia (mint family: square stems, scented leaves)
Eupatorium or Ageratina (boneset, snakeroot)
Chrysanthemum cutting

A flower (stevia has small white flowers in autumn)

scientific_name: Philodendron 'Ring of Fire' (sold as Philodendron serratum)
id_basis: Split from P-055: Ethan says this photo shows a different plant from the Black Cardinal. A broad, glossy, oval leaf marbled lime and yellow over green, on a long stalk from the base, so probably a self-heading philodendron. Not enough to name it from one photo.

The HEB tag in the pot reads 'Philodendron Ring of Fire, Philodendron serratum', and the clearance label 'HEB PHILO RNG OF FIRE 5IN'. Its leaves are marbled lime and yellow over green, which is how 'Ring of Fire' looks; young leaves are smooth-edged and later ones become long and jagged.
id_alternatives:
Philodendron 'Calypso' (lime-and-yellow marbled)
Philodendron 'Painted Lady' (young leaf)
Philodendron 'Golden Crocodile'
Philodendron 'Prince of Orange' (green-leaf stage)
